questions: For n < 0, what should the function return? Should it raise an error, return a sentinel value, or follow some extended recurrence?
Is the function required to handle very large n (e.g., beyond Python int range, or causing performance issues) and if so, should it use approximation or return modulo something?
Should the function return an exact integer for all n, or is an approximate floating-point result acceptable when n is large?
Is the function allowed to use iterative loops with O(n) time, or must it use a more efficient method (e.g., matrix exponentiation) for better performance?
Should the function cache intermediate results across multiple calls (memoization), or is each call independent?
If n is not an integer (e.g., float), should the function cast to int, raise an error, or handle differently?
Does 'without recursion' prohibit any recursive technique, including indirect recursion or using recursion in helper functions?
Should the function compute fib4(n) for n up to which the recurrence holds exactly, or is there a maximum n beyond which approximation is required?
